guides.title: Termite Inspection Cost in Orlando, FL (2026 Guide)
guides.metaDescription: What a termite inspection costs in Orlando: free sales inspections vs. paid WDO reports for closings, what moves the price, and what to ask before you book.
guides.h1: Termite Inspection Cost in Orlando, FL
intro: "Termite inspection" means two different things in Orlando, and they are priced very differently. One is a free visit a pest company makes before quoting treatment. The other is a paid, dated wood-destroying organism (WDO) report that a lender or closing asks for.
This guide explains which one you need, what drives the price, and what to ask before anyone walks your home.

sections.heading: Free inspection vs. a paid WDO report
body: If you think you have termites and want a treatment quote, most pest-control companies inspect for free, because the visit ends in a quote for treatment.

If you are buying, selling or refinancing, the lender or closing usually needs a WDO report. In Florida that report goes on the state form FDACS-13645, filled out by a licensed inspector. It is a dated document with your property address, so it is billed as its own service.
A general home inspection is not the same thing. Home-inspector standards of practice exclude wood-destroying organisms, so termites are usually left out unless you add a WDO inspection.

sections.heading: What a WDO inspection typically costs
body: Few Florida companies publish a price; most quote by phone based on square footage. A July 2026 survey of advertised prices from licensed Florida companies put a typical single-family WDO inspection at about $75 to $200, with a median around $125 and a full spread of about $50 to $275 or more.
Published Central Florida prices in that survey ran roughly $99 to $250. Some inspectors charge less when the WDO is added to a home inspection in the same visit than when it is booked on its own.
Treat these as reference points for your calls, not a quote. Ask for the price in writing before you book.

sections.heading: What moves the price
body: Home size is the main driver. Price lists usually use a base price up to around 2,000 to 3,000 square feet and add a fee above that.
Crawlspaces, detached garages, sheds and extra structures add time. Older Orlando homes with wood framing, raised floors or additions also take longer to walk than newer slab homes.
A tight closing date can matter. Ask whether same-day or next-day service costs extra before you book it.

sections.heading: What to ask before you book
body: Ask whether the visit is a free treatment estimate or a WDO report on the Florida form, so you get the document your lender actually needs.
Confirm the inspector's company is licensed by the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS), and ask how quickly the written report is delivered.
If activity or damage is found, ask what a re-inspection or clearance letter costs and whether any inspection fee is credited toward treatment.

sections.heading: Signs worth an inspection in Central Florida
body: Subterranean termites are the common problem around Orlando. Watch for pencil-wide mud tubes on slab edges, foundation walls or garage stem walls.
Spring swarms of winged insects, or piles of shed wings on window sills, are another strong sign. So are baseboards or door frames that sound hollow or blister when pressed.
Drywood termites leave small piles of pellet-like droppings below infested wood. If you see any of these, an inspection and treatment quote is the next step.

faqs.question: Is a termite inspection free in Orlando?
faqs.answer: A treatment estimate usually is. A WDO report for a sale, refinance or closing is a separate paid service, typically priced by home size.

faqs.question: Does a home inspection include termites?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Home-inspector standards exclude wood-destroying organisms, so you need a separate WDO inspection if your lender or closing asks for one.

faqs.question: What form is used for a Florida WDO inspection?
faqs.answer: Florida uses state form FDACS-13645, completed by a licensed inspector. Some lenders also ask for the national NPMA-33, but Florida's form is the standard here.

faqs.question: How long does a termite inspection take?
faqs.answer: For a typical single-family home, usually about an hour or less on site. Larger homes, crawlspaces and outbuildings take longer.

guides.title: Mosquito Control in Orlando, FL: A Homeowner's Guide
guides.metaDescription: Mosquito control in Orlando: where mosquitoes breed on a typical lot, what yard treatments do, how often they are usually repeated, and what to check before hiring.
guides.h1: Mosquito Control in Orlando, FL: A Homeowner's Guide
intro: Orlando's warm, wet months give mosquitoes a long season, and most of the bites in a backyard come from mosquitoes that bred within a short distance of the house.
This guide covers what you can fix yourself, what professional yard treatments do, and what to ask before you sign up for a service.

sections.heading: Start with standing water
body: Container mosquitoes such as the Asian tiger mosquito and the yellow fever mosquito breed in very small amounts of water, even a bottle cap's worth. Once a week, tip and toss anything that holds water: plant saucers, buckets, toys, tarps and wheelbarrows.

Check clogged gutters, French-drain grates, downspout extensions and low spots that stay wet after a storm. Bromeliads, which are popular in Central Florida landscaping, hold water in their leaves and can breed mosquitoes too. Flush them with a hose or thin them out.
Keep pools chlorinated and filtered, and change birdbath and pet-bowl water at least weekly.

sections.heading: What a yard treatment does
body: Most residential mosquito services spray a barrier treatment on shaded foliage, under decks and along fence lines, where adult mosquitoes rest during the day. They often add a larvicide to water that can't be dumped.

Barrier treatments wear off with time, rain and new plant growth, so they are usually repeated on a schedule through the warm season. Ask how often visits happen, what product is used, and what happens if heavy rain falls right after a visit.
If anyone in the home keeps bees, fish ponds or sensitive plants, say so up front so the treatment plan can account for them.

sections.heading: County mosquito control vs. your yard
body: Orange County and Osceola County both run public mosquito-control programs that monitor and treat at the neighborhood level. Those programs don't treat individual backyards, so the containers and shady resting spots on your own lot are still on you or a private service.
If your street has a standing-water problem in a public drainage area, report it to your county's mosquito-control office.

sections.heading: What to ask before hiring
body: Confirm the company holds a Florida pest-control license from FDACS. Ask for the visit frequency, the product names, and how long the service agreement runs before you sign.
Ask whether the technician also inspects for and removes breeding sites, or only sprays. The best results come from doing both.
Get the price and cancellation terms in writing.

faqs.question: When is mosquito season in Orlando?
faqs.answer: Mosquitoes are most active in the warm, rainy months, roughly late spring through fall, but in Central Florida's mild climate they can show up any time temperatures stay warm.

faqs.question: How often are mosquito yard treatments repeated?
faqs.answer: Barrier treatments break down with rain, sun and plant growth, so most services repeat them on a regular schedule during the warm season. Ask the provider for their interval before signing.

faqs.question: Will the county spray my backyard?
faqs.answer: No. Orange and Osceola County mosquito-control programs work at the neighborhood level and don't treat individual yards, so breeding sites on your lot still need attention.

faqs.question: Do bug zappers or citronella candles work?
faqs.answer: They do little to lower biting numbers in a yard. Removing standing water and treating shady resting areas work better.
